replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

- Automated abuse of reachable endpoints: design says "The portal is reachable from the internet" but describes no password form, sign-up, email/SMS send or data-returning page; the exposure/credential-attack angle is already covered by listed threat 3 — not a distinct gap.
- Staff screens showing content other people supply: design mentions no comments, files, tickets or profile fields — not present.
- Privileged actions with no record of who did it: design says "the portal reads the role attribute from the assertion to decide admin access" for an "internal admin portal" and states no logging of logins or admin actions — not covered by any listed threat (all seven are Spoofing/Tampering/ElevationOfPrivilege about assertion validation and role freshness).
- Personal/financial documents cacheable by browsers or CDNs: no documents or pages of that kind described — not present.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, exports, emails or headers: design describes no logging, export, email or header sink — not present.
- Single-reviewer items: audience/issuer checks, IdP pinning, stale roles, XML parsing wrapping and login probing are all restatements or build-detail variants of listed threats 1, 4, 6, 7 and 3 — none included.

  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-05",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["internal admin portal", "SAML assertion consumer", "role attribute check", "corporate identity provider"],
    "dataStores": [],
    "externalServices": ["corporate identity provider"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["internet to internal admin portal", "portal to corporate IdP"],
    "dataClasses": ["credentials"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No record of who signed in as admin or what they changed in the portal",
      "scenario": "The design grants admin access in an internet-facing portal purely from an assertion attribute and names no audit log of logins, the identity and role attribute accepted, or the administrative actions taken. An employee, or an attacker who reached admin through any of the assertion flaws, can change portal data or settings and later deny it; the organisation cannot tell a forged or replayed login from a genuine one, so abuse and compromise go unnoticed and cannot be investigated.",
      "component": "internal admin portal (SSO login and admin actions)",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 2,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "After login, the portal reads the role attribute from the assertion to decide admin access. The portal is reachable from the internet." },
        { "quote": "Employees sign in to the internal admin portal through SAML single sign-on with the corporate identity provider." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.3", "V7.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Admin logins and admin actions in the portal are not recorded, so nobody can prove who did what or spot a stolen admin session.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Audit admin authentication and privileged actions",
        "given": "an employee authenticates to the internet-facing admin portal via SAML and is granted admin access from the role attribute",
        "when": "the login is accepted and any administrative action is performed",
        "then": "the portal writes a tamper-resistant audit record of the asserted identity, issuer, role attribute, timestamp, source address and the action performed, retained and reviewable independently of the acting admin"
      }
    }
  ]
}
